name: Anchored run → re-wake coordinator to begin the dev loop (decide dev_from_task)
description:
Dev-loop kickoff, half 2 of 2. Once rule 01 has stamped the bare agent.loop.run anchor on the resumed run AND the projection station (dev-from-task/03) has frozen the change's tasks into task.spec, this rule spawns a fresh coordinator loop bound to that run and lets it RE-DECIDE the arc — the human approved the change, so the coordinator's job now is to route into development (decide(dev_from_task)). The task.spec.test-command ne "" condition gates this re-wake behind projection completion: the coordinator's prompt tells it to read the projected task specs, so they must exist first, and gating on the projected fact (rather than firing in parallel with projection) serializes the two forced-tool turns so the journey's positional cursor is not raced. This is the semdev 'coordinator re-decides each wake' pattern (semteams coordinator/30-plan-walking) applied at the approval→dev boundary.

READINESS GATE (SB5, design group 5): the sandbox.provision.ready eq true condition gates this re-wake behind the provision-and-prove-cold station (sandbox/01-provision → provision_sandbox). The dev loop proceeds ONLY once a sandbox-scope tier has PROVEN the claim on a cold-built environment; an unprovable sandbox stamps sandbox.provision.blocked (never sandbox.provision.ready), so this rule does not fire and sandbox/02-park-unprovable parks the run instead. This is the make-or-break gate — no dispatch, measurement, or verify happens over an absent/unproven sandbox (the semspec disease). It also sequences the provision turn before the decide turn (provision is gated on projection, this on provision → project_tasks → provision_sandbox → decide). When the dedicated developer dispatch lands (g7 dispatch-developer), the same sandbox.provision.ready gate moves onto it.

Run binding: run_scope=inherit reads the run entity's bare agent.loop.run triple (stamped by rule 01) and sets the spawned coordinator's RunID to it, so the coordinator is a real lifecycle member of THIS run — its decision, and any dispatch rule that later inherits off it, resolve the same run. related_loops threads run-loop-entity-id=$entity.id so the coordinator can query_entity the run to read the projected task specs. This is DISTINCT from run_scope=new: no second run is minted (the dual-anchor guard is not tripped — inherit is not a minter).

action_allowlist scopes the decide DECISION to [dev_from_task, ask_human] (route into development, or escalate). tools advertises a SCOPED list [decide, query_entity, read_loop_result, scratchpad] (decide + read tools only, never create_change/forge-io), matching the front-door/mint re-wakes — the effective control at the model boundary (a provider only emits advertised tools). NOTE MEDIUM-3 (the EXECUTOR-side backstop for this advertised list) LANDED in beta.149 (semstreams #551): agentic-tools admitToolCall now rejects a call outside the loop's advertised set (stamped as agent.tools.advertised from the loop's cached tools), so this scoped list is enforced at EXECUTION, not just advertised. action_allowlist still gates the decide arg; the tools list now gates which tool is called. Regression-guarded by TestTripwireExecutorHonorsPerLoopToolAllowlist; no longer blocks the first real-LLM token.

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps the fired-once marker run.dev.kickoff=$entity.instance on the run, and the run.dev.kickoff length_eq 0 guard makes the trigger flip false the moment it fires. This is the semteams agent-run/02 discipline (a top-level condition its own action extinguishes) — publish_agent is NOT idempotent (each fire mints a fresh loop; the framework does not dedup), and the other trigger conditions (agent.loop.run/executing/approved) stay true, so WITHOUT this marker a graph replay with no persisted rule-state (RULE_STATE wiped while ENTITY_STATES survives — asymmetric bucket loss) would re-spawn a DUPLICATE coordinator. The marker (a durable ENTITY_STATES triple) closes that: on any re-scan the guard reads it present and the rule does not re-fire, independent of RULE_STATE. Deterministic object ($entity.instance) so a re-write is idempotent. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish so a publish failure leaves the run stuck-toward-human rather than duplicated. Subsequent coordinator re-wakes are LOOP-terminal-driven (dispatch-developer's worker terminal → coordinator), not run-entity-driven. G2: this fires no lifecycle transition.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt:
SEMDEV COORDINATOR — the human approved the generated change and the run resumed to executing. Begin developing the run's tasks.

Your run entity ID is $entity.id. Read its state with query_entity(entity_id="$entity.id") — the projected task specs (task.spec.<i>.*) and any progress markers (task.attempt.<i>, review.verdict.<i>). Choose the single next station and record it with the decide tool: one action from your closed taxonomy plus a short reason.

- To develop the next task, decide(action="dev_from_task", reason="<which task / why>"). A dispatch rule then spawns a developer for it.
- If the run cannot proceed (no projected tasks, a blocking gap), decide(action="ask_human", reason="<what you need>").

Do not do the work yourself — your job is to route.

metadata.station: dev-loop kickoff (2/2) — re-wake coordinator → decide dev_from_task
metadata.run_binding: run_scope=inherit reads the run entity's agent.loop.run (stamped by rule 01) → spawned coordinator's RunID = the run id → it carries agent.loop.run + agent.run.entity-id, a real lifecycle member. NOT run_scope=new (no second run minted).
metadata.projection_gate: task.spec.test-command ne "" gates this re-wake behind dev-from-task/03 (project_tasks) completion, so the coordinator reads projected specs and the two forced-tool turns (project_tasks, then decide) do not race the journey's positional cursor. task 0 always exists (Project stamps contiguous 0..n-1, >=1 task) and test_command is a required task.spec field, so it is a reliable projection-complete signal.
metadata.readiness_gate: sandbox.provision.ready eq true gates this re-wake behind the provision-and-prove-cold station (sandbox/01-provision → provision_sandbox), SB5. The dev loop proceeds only on a PROVEN sandbox-scope tier; an unprovable sandbox stamps sandbox.provision.blocked (never sandbox.provision.ready) so this rule does not fire and sandbox/02-park-unprovable parks the run. This is the make-or-break gate (no dispatch/measure/verify over an absent sandbox). It also serializes the provision turn before the decide turn. Pinned by TestDevRewakeGatedOnSandboxReadiness; the dedicated dispatch gate lands with g7 dispatch-developer.
metadata.action_allowlist: decide scoped to [dev_from_task, ask_human]. tools advertises the scoped [decide, query_entity, read_loop_result, scratchpad] set (matches the front-door/mint re-wakes; enforced offline by TestEveryModelSpawnDeclaresToolsAllowlist / TestRuleToolsSubsetOfAllowed). MEDIUM-3 (the EXECUTOR-side backstop) LANDED in beta.149 (semstreams #551): the executor now enforces the loop's advertised set (agent.tools.advertised), so this scoped tools list is load-bearing at execution. Regression-guarded by TestTripwireExecutorHonorsPerLoopToolAllowlist.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the run.dev.kickoff marker + length_eq 0 guard (semteams agent-run/02 pattern). publish_agent is not idempotent, so this makes the one-shot intrinsic (not reliant on the durable RULE_STATE bucket) — a duplicate coordinator cannot be spawned even under asymmetric RULE_STATE loss. Proven by TestSpineJourneyRestartDoesNotReplay. NOTE the sibling publish_agent spawn rules coordinator/02, coordinator/03, and run-lifecycle/03 are NOT yet self-extinguishing — they rely on RULE_STATE durability alone (safe on a normal restart, exposed under asymmetric bucket loss); pull the same marker pattern forward before production (see design.md D15/restart-safety note).
